text.p: Sherwin-Williams Co said it is pleased with the contributions that are beginning to be made by its acquisitions as the integration process continues.
The operating profit contributions during 1996 from Pratt & Lambert United Inc and its other acquisitions exceeded the related cost of financing the acquisitions, the company said.

"We expect 1997 to be another challenging year for the company as we continue to integrate the recent acquisitions and begin to integrate the operations of Thompson Minwax Holding Corp, which was just acquired in January 1997," chief executive John Breen said.
Sherwin-Williams said other segments also showed continuing improvement.
Net sales in the Paint Stores segment were $2.41 billion for 1996, up 13.1 percent over the last year, with comparable-store sales up 10.0 percent.
Excluding the effects of acquisitions, Paint Stores' sales for the year increased 9.1 percent, primarily due to increased paint gallons sold, the company said.
The Paint Stores segment's annual operating profit increased 30.2 percent to $206.3 million and increased 28.1 percent when excluding the effects of acquisitions.
Operating profits increased as a result of volume gains and the continuing containment of selling and administrative costs, the company said.
The Coatings segment's annual net sales increased 51.4 percent to $1.71 billion from $1.13 billion last year.
Operating profits of the Coatings segment increased 28.3 percent for the year to $259.7 million, the company said.
Excluding the effects of acquisitions, the Coatings segment's sales increased 4.7 percent year-to-date.

Operating profits of the Coatings Segment, excluding acquisitions, increased 11.9 percent due to containment of administrative expenditures and manufacturing efficiencies resulting from increased gallon sales, the company said.
In the fourth quarter, the Paint Stores segment had a sales gain of 9.9 percent and a 41.0 percent operating profit improvement, excluding acquisitions.
The Coatings segment's sales rose 5.1 percent in the fourth quarter and operating profit excluding acquisitions rose 23.1 percent.
"The company had another good year in 1996 and continued its track record of achieving record sales and earnings," Breen said.

"The acquisitions made during 1995 and 1996 in the U.S. and Latin America, the largest of which was Pratt & Lambert United Inc, gave the company several important brands and operations and provided the company with further growth opportunities in the dealer, mass merchandiser, automotive and specialty markets," he said.
